R5-255500 Agenda - opening session Type: agenda For: Information Source: WG Chairman Discussion: The RAN5 Chair openend the meeting. AT&T welcomed on behalf of the host all delegates to the RAN5#109 meeting in Dallas and presented the practicalities. Then the RAN5 Chair reminded: Reminder for IPR declaration "The attention of the delegates to the meeting of this Technical Specification Group was drawn to the fact that 3GPP Individual Members have the obligation under the IPR Policies of their respective Organizational Partners to inform their respective Organizational Partners of Essential IPRs they become aware of. The delegates were asked to take note that they were thereby invited: to investigate whether their organization or any other organization owns IPRs which were, or were likely to become Essential in respect of the work of 3GPP. to notify their respective Organizational Partners of all potential IPRs, e.g., for ETSI, by means of the IPR Information Statement and the Licensing declaration forms " Antitrust Guidance "The attention of the delegates to the meeting was drawn to the fact that 3GPP activities were subject to all applicable antitrust and competition laws and that compliance with said laws was therefore required by any participant of the meeting, including the Chair and Vice-Chairs and were invited to seek any clarification needed with their legal counsel. The leadership would conduct the present meeting with impartiality and in the interests of 3GPP. Delegates were reminded that timely submission of work items in advance of TSG/WG/SWG meetings was important to allow for full and fair consideration of such matters." R5-181125 Agenda - opening session Type: agenda For: Information Source: WG Chairman (Replaces R5-180200) Discussion: The RAN5 Chair opened the RAN5#78 meeting in Athens, Greece and welcomed all delegates thanking the European Friends of 3GPP for hosting. Vodafone welcomed on behalf of the European Friends of 3GPP all delegates to the venue and explained the meeting facilities. Then the RAN5 Chair presented the agenda. The RAN5 Chair then reminded the delegates about the ETSI IPR policy: - The attention of the members of this Technical Specification Group is drawn to the fact that 3GPP Individual Members have the obligation under the IPR Policies of their respective Organizational Partners to inform their respective Organizational Partners of Essential IPRs they become aware of. The members take note that they are hereby invited: - to investigate in their company whether their company does own IPRs which are, or are likely to become Essential in respect of the work of the Technical Specification Group. - to notify the Director-General, or the Chairman of their respective Organisational Partners, of all potential IPRs that their company may own, by means of the IPR Statement and the Licensing declaration forms (e.g. See the ETSI IPR forms http://webapp.etsi.org/Ipr/). The RAN5 chair also explained: “I also draw your attention to the fact that 3GPP activities are subject to antitrust and competition laws and that compliance with said laws is therefore required of any participant of this TSG/WG meeting including the Chairman and Vice Chairman. In case of question I recommend that you contact your legal counsel. The present meeting will be conducted with strict impartiality and in the interests of 3GPP. There was no welcome from the host. Then the RAN5 Chair presented the agenda. The RAN5 Chair then reminded the delegates about the ETSI IPR policy: - The attention of the members of this Technical Specification Group is drawn to the fact that 3GPP Individual Members have the obligation under the IPR Policies of their respective Organizational Partners to inform their respective Organizational Partners of Essential IPRs they become aware of. The worksheets "NR bands" and "5G NR CADC Configurations" include lists showing the current status for RAN5 NR bands, NR band CBW extensions and 5G NR CADC configurations for power class 3 (PC3) and applicable additional power classes (e.g. PC1.5 and PC2). The list shows for each NR band, NR band CBW extensions and 5G NR CADC configuration the declared interested operator and the company that have been assigned taking for adding necessary details to 3GPP RAN5 UE conformance test specifications for PC3. Interested operator for other power than PC3 is tracked within the specific work plan of the power class. The list also shows the Work Item code (s) to be used when submitting CRs for the different NR bands and 5G NR CADC configurations for the different power classes. The status is updated after each RAN5 meeting. The NR bands and 5G NR CADC configurations worksheets provides tools to select one or more NR bands/5G NR CADC configurations for the purpose to request assignment as interested operator and/or responsible company of NR bands, NR band CBW extensions and 5G NR CADC configuration(s). For guideline how to use the NR bands and 5G NR CADC configurations worksheets see the PRD21 word document. R5-205020 Agenda - opening session Type: agenda For: Information Source: WG Chairman Discussion: Reminder for IPR declaration The RAN5 Chair drew the attention to the delegates' obligations under the 3GPP Partner Organizations’ IPR policies. Every Individual Member organization is obliged to declare to the Partner Organization or Organizations of which it is a member any IPR owned by the Individual Member or any other organization which is or is likely to become essential to the work of 3GPP. Delegates are asked to take note that they are thereby invited: • to investigate whether their organization or any other organization owns IPRs which were, or were likely to become Essential in respect of the work of 3GPP. • to notify their respective Organizational Partners of all potential IPRs, e.g., for ETSI, by means of the IPR Information Statement and the Licensing declaration forms (e.g. see the ETSI IPR forms http://webapp.etsi.org/Ipr/). Antitrust Guidance The RAN5 Chair drew the delegates' attention to the fact that 3GPP activities are subject to all applicable antitrust and competition laws and that compliance with said laws is therefore required of any participant of this TSG/WG meeting including the Chairman and Vice Chairman. In case of question it is recommended that you contact your legal counsel. The leadership shall conduct the present meeting with impartiality and in the interests of 3GPP. Furthermore, the timely submission of work items in advance of TSG/WG meetings is important to allow for full and fair consideration of such matters.” http://www.3gpp.org/about-3gpp/legal-matters/21-3gpp-calendar/1616-statement-of-antitrust-compliance Decision: The document was revised to R5-206242. he RAN5 Status Report and CR Review RP-240871 Noted MCX Server Conformance Testing CT#104 accepted the proposal submitted in CP-241276 for 3GPP to undertake MCX Server Conformance Test Development and sent a LS to RAN stating the same in CP-241302 (RP-240899) RP#104 considered CT input received via the LS along with the proposals submitted in RP-241517 and made the decision: RAN5 to take up MCX Server Conformance Test Development. RP#104 tasked RAN5 to submit updated ToR for approval to RP#105. RP-240872 All CRs packs (except CR packs RP-240952 and RP-240953, see details below) approved. CR Pack – RP-240952 - Partially Approved (all CRs of RP-240952 are approved except R5-243395) R5-243395 was revised in replacement company CR RP-241590 (Qualcomm) and was approved. CR Pack – RP-240953 - Partially Approved (all CRs of RP-240953 are approved except R5-243648) R5-243648 (CR reserved for TS 38.521-1 agreed and submitted with incorrect contents of a CR to TR 38.905. CR author incorrectly used contents of R5-242429 (CR to TR 38.905) to create the final version - R5-243648, which was the final tdoc assigned to TS 38.521-1 CR R5-242529. MCC TF 160 RP-240873 The TF 160 report No comments Approved Status Reports - all noted and any changes to TCD and updated WIDs were approved Thank you to all WI rapporteurs for reserving and submitting Status Reports on time. Unfortunately, Qualcomm and CMCC submitted revised WIDs for ‘Support of Uncrewed Aerial Systems Connectivity, Identification, and Tracking’ and ‘High power UE (power class 1.5) for NR FR1 TDD single band’ respectively with TCD not being updated to RP#104 (Jun-24) as these WIs got completed at this meeting. Nokia’ submitted revised WID for ‘XR (eXtended Reality) enhancements for NR plus CT1 aspects’ with the tdoc header field ‘Document For:’ - ‘Endorsement’ instead of ‘Approval’. Same issue in the Qualcomm new Conformance WID for ‘Requirement for NR frequency range 2 (FR2) multi-Rx chain DL reception’. All of these led to intervention by the RAN Secretary causing tdocs to be revised and to be handled during the meeting instead of being concluded under block agreement. Needless to say, these misdemeanors by WI rapporteurs reflect poorly on RAN5, which must be avoided in the future. . he RAN5 Status Report and CR Review RP-240871 Noted MCX Server Conformance Testing CT#104 accepted the proposal submitted in CP-241276 for 3GPP to undertake MCX Server Conformance Test Development and sent a LS to RAN stating the same in CP-241302 (RP-240899) RP#104 considered CT input received via the LS along with the proposals submitted in RP-241517 and made the decision: RAN5 to take up MCX Server Conformance Test Development. RP#104 tasked RAN5 to submit updated ToR for approval to RP#105. RP-240872 All CRs packs (except CR packs RP-240952 and RP-240953, see details below) approved. CR Pack – RP-240952 - Partially Approved (all CRs of RP-240952 are approved except R5-243395) R5-243395 was revised in replacement company CR RP-241590 (Qualcomm) and was approved. CR Pack – RP-240953 - Partially Approved (all CRs of RP-240953 are approved except R5-243648) R5-243648 (CR reserved for TS 38.521-1 agreed and submitted with incorrect contents of a CR to TR 38.905. CR author incorrectly used contents of R5-242429 (CR to TR 38.905) to create the final version - R5-243648, which was the final tdoc assigned to TS 38.521-1 CR R5-242529. MCC TF 160 RP-240873 The TF 160 report No comments Approved Status Reports - all noted and any changes to TCD and updated WIDs were approved Thank you to all WI rapporteurs for reserving and submitting Status Reports on time. Unfortunately, Qualcomm and CMCC submitted revised WIDs for ‘Support of Uncrewed Aerial Systems Connectivity, Identification, and Tracking’ and ‘High power UE (power class 1.5) for NR FR1 TDD single band’ respectively with TCD not being updated to RP#104 (Jun-24) as these WIs got completed at this meeting. Nokia’ submitted revised WID for ‘XR (eXtended Reality) enhancements for NR plus CT1 aspects’ with the tdoc header field ‘Document For:’ - ‘Endorsement’ instead of ‘Approval’. Same issue in the Qualcomm new Conformance WID for ‘Requirement for NR frequency range 2 (FR2) multi-Rx chain DL reception’. All of these led to intervention by the RAN Secretary causing tdocs to be revised and to be handled during the meeting instead of being concluded under block agreement. Needless to say, these misdemeanors by WI rapporteurs reflect poorly on RAN5, which must be avoided in the future. . RAN5 Work Item Proposals – all approved ITU-R ad hoc RP-240875 Status Report ITU-R Ad hoc from ITU-R Ad Hoc convenor for information and noted. Topics for RAN5 Interest: Rel-18 ASN.1 Review fully completed and considered frozen. 5G NR RAN Groups Status RAN1: NR Rel-15 very stable – no correction CR NR Rel-16 very stable – 4 corrections CRs NR Rel-17 stable – 12 corrections CRs NR Rel-18 - 3 Cat B CRs (NR NTN) and 83 correction CRs RAN2: NR Rel-15 very stable – 5 correction CRs ((NR_newRAT-Core) NR Rel-16 very stable – 7 correction CRs (NR_newRAT-Core, 5G_V2X_NRSL-Core, NR_UE_pow_sav-Core, NR_HST; NR_pos-Core) NR Rel-17 stable – 36 correction CRs (NR_newRAT-Core ; NR_IIOT-Core; NR_cov_enh-Core; NR_FeMIMO-Core; NR_ENDC_SON_MDT_enh-Core; NR_FeMIMO-Core; NR_NTN_solutions-Core; NR_IIOT_URLLC_enh-Core; NR_redcap-Core; NR_SmallData_INACTIVE-Core; NR_SL_relay-Core) NR Rel-18 - All WIs completed (Completed all UE capability/feature group implementation) 20 Cat B (NR_Mob_enh2-Core; NR_FR1_lessthan_5MHz , TEI18…. ) and 66 correction CRs RAN4: , Rel-15 RF Core / RRM Core / RRM Performance maintenance – Only essential corrections agreed (very high threshold applied), reduction in number of maintenance CRs Rel-16 NR: Core and Performance parts completed, now under maintenance Rel-17 NR: Core and Performance Parts completed, now under maintenance Rel-18 NR Core part completed, Performance part completed except for ‘NR_pos_enh2-Perf’ and ‘NR_FR1_TRP_TRS_enh-Perf’ WIs RAN4 Spec Quality R5-240782 Endorsed way forward to improve quality of RAN4 s
